title: The Fire and the Waterman
theme: Five stops through the burning City with Will Chandler, a Thames waterman, in the first week of September 1666. The fire begins in a baker's house and takes four days, and the men who make their living rowing the river spend it carrying other people's lives out of it.

companion.name: Will Chandler
companion.brief: Forty-two, a licensed waterman who served his seven years and rows a pair of oars from Old Swan Stairs. Born in Southwark. Dry, steady, unimpressed by gentlemen. He carried furniture, plate and frightened families downriver through the fire of September 1666, and charged what the day was worth, which he will admit to. He knows the river's tides and stairs the way other men know streets, and nothing at all of the world past Gravesend.

presence.standing: at the top of Old Swan Stairs with his wherry moored below, the river and the crowded bridge behind him
presence.gesture: rubs his palms together against the cold

style.look: Photographic realism as if a camera had stood in London in September 1666: timber-framed jettied houses, narrow lanes, smoke-filled orange light, ash falling, the river crowded with lighters and wherries. Period clothing of the Restoration, wide hats, breeches, coifs. Portrait 9:16 framing, eye level. Muted colour under smoke, not sepia.
style.avoid: no Georgian or Victorian buildings, no Wren's St Paul's dome (built after this), no Tower Bridge, no embankments, no gas or electric light, no modern clothing or vehicles, no text overlays

stops.title: Pudding Lane
stops.brief: The narrow lane behind Thames Street where the fire started in a baker's house before dawn on the second of September. Timber houses jettied out overhead almost touching, cellars full of pitch and oil.
mustCover: how the fire began and how fast it moved
why the houses burned so easily
archiveQueries: London before the Great Fire houses

stops.title: Old Swan Stairs
stops.brief: The waterman's own stairs on the north bank just above the bridge, where the lighters and wherries loaded goods away from the fire and where fares went from pennies to pounds in a day.
mustCover: what watermen did during the fire and what they charged
how the stairs and the river worked
what people carried away with them

stops.title: London Bridge
stops.brief: The only bridge, crowded with houses and shops, its northern end burning. The gap left by the fire of 1633 is what stopped the flames crossing to Southwark.
mustCover: the houses on the bridge and who lived there

stops.title: Old St Paul's
stops.brief: The medieval cathedral, scaffolded for repair, its roof lead running molten into the churchyard and the booksellers' stock burning in the crypt of St Faith's beneath it.
mustCover: what the old cathedral looked like
the booksellers and what they lost
archiveQueries: Old St Pauls burning Great Fire
St Faith's under St Paul's booksellers

stops.title: Moorfields
stops.brief: The open fields north of the wall where tens of thousands camped with what they saved, in tents and under carts, while the City burned out behind them.
mustCover: the camps and what people had with them
prices for bread and carts after the fire
what happens to the city next
